credentials.description: API key from the Wave Business portal (sent as Authorization: Bearer); it is tied to a real wallet — Wave documents no sandbox

parameters.name: date
parameters.description: Date in YYYY-MM-DD format. If absent, returns the current day's transactions.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: Opaque pagination cursor. Pass the end_cursor value from the previous response to get the next page.

parameters.name: first
parameters.description: The maximum number of items to retrieve. The server may respond with fewer items if your limit is too high, or if there aren't enough items remaining to fulfill the request. Optional: without it, the server will choose a sensible default.

example_prompt: Get my recent Wave wallet transactions.

has_next_page.description: true if there are transactions left to fetch.

end_cursor.description: Cursor to pass as the after parameter to get the next page.

date.description: Date of the returned transactions, in YYYY-MM-DD format.

items.description: List of transactions, sorted from oldest to newest.

timestamp.description: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp of the transaction's execution.

amount.description: Net balance change (can be negative for debits).

is_reversal.description: true if the transaction is a refund or reversal.

counterparty_name.description: Name of the sender or recipient.

client_reference.description: Internal reference provided when the payment was created.

checkout_api_session_id.description: ID of the associated checkout session (for api_checkout).

balance.description: Wallet balance after this transaction. Useful for line-by-line reconciliation.

payment_reason.description: Payment reason provided by the sender.

custom_fields.description: Key-value metadata associated with the transaction.

submerchant_id.description: Sub-account identifier if include_subaccounts is enabled.

government_tax_paid_by_wave.description: Tax amount covered by Wave (Senegal only).

business_user_name.description: Name of the agent or depositary associated with the transaction.

business_user_mobile.description: Phone number of the agent or depositary.

employee_id.description: Employee identifier associated with the transaction.

submerchant_name.description: Sub-account name if include_subaccounts is enabled.

details.description: Validation details returned on request-validation-error. Each entry contains loc (field location), msg (message), type (error type). Can be null or absent (measured on 2026-10-24 on 401 errors) — check before iterating.

gotchas: Transactions are returned from oldest to newest for a given day. To get the most recent transactions first, reverse the array client-side.
Without a date parameter, Wave returns only the current day's transactions (UTC). For reconciliation, always specify the date explicitly.
Pagination uses opaque cursors (end_cursor), not offsets. Do not build the cursor manually — use only the value returned by the API.
To fetch all of a day's transactions, loop while page_info.has_next_page === true, passing end_cursor as the after parameter.

If the API key was created with request signing (optional Business Portal setting), every call must carry Wave-Signature: t={timestamp},v1={HMAC-SHA256(timestamp + raw body)} computed with the signing secret (format wave_sn_AKS_…, shown only once) — empty body for a GET. Without it: 401 missing-signature; other codes: invalid-signature, invalid-signature-format, invalid-signature-timestamp, expired-signature-timestamp (timestamp more than 5 minutes in the past or more than 30 seconds in the future). The setting is permanent for a key: to drop it, revoke the key and create another one.

[MUST TELL USER] The API IP whitelist turns on as soon as the first address is added in the Business Portal (Developer section) and can no longer be turned off from the portal — you have to go through your Wave account manager. Calls from an unlisted IP get 403 ip-not-allowed: on hosting without a fixed outbound IP (serverless functions, most PaaS), do not add any IP before you have a fixed egress.
open_questions: first comes from Wave's general Pagination section ("The server will choose a sensible default for the collection being retrieved"); the GET /v1/transactions parameter table lists only date, after and include_subaccounts: does /v1/transactions accept first?
